tagline: Home of the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat, gateway to the eastern mountains
introHtml: Phitsanulok is the big city of the lower North, and plenty of people just use it as a pit stop on the way up to Chiang Mai. But there's more here than you'd guess. Most come to pay respects to the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, a Buddha image many rank among the most beautiful in Thailand. The town sits along the Nan River, so an evening stroll by the water is easy and pleasant, and there are well-known eats like the "dangling-legs" noodles and flying morning glory to try. Head out of town toward Nakhon Thai and Chat Trakan districts and you hit the mountains, waterfalls, and flower fields of the national parks, which carry on all the way to Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek.
bestTime: November–February is cool and clear, easy for exploring the town and heading up the mountains around Nakhon Thai. In the cold season, Phu Hin Rong Kla also gets its wild Himalayan cherry blossoms.

highlights.name: Phra Phuttha Chinnarat at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat
highlights.blurb: The city's revered Buddha image, widely called one of the most beautiful in Thailand. Almost everyone visiting Phitsanulok stops here to pay respects.

highlights.name: Nan riverfront
highlights.blurb: The main river runs right through the middle of town, with a riverside walk, bridges, and an evening market for catching the breeze after sunset.

highlights.name: Dangling-legs noodles (kuai tiao hoi kha)
highlights.blurb: Noodle shops along the Nan River where you sit on the bank with your legs hanging over the edge. It's a classic Phitsanulok thing people love trying.

highlights.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla National Park
highlights.blurb: The mountains around Nakhon Thai, with the cracked-rock field, Pha Chu Thong cliff, and wild cherry blossoms in the cold season. A popular spot for nature.

highlights.name: Thung Salaeng Luang National Park
highlights.blurb: A wide savanna grassland some call Thailand's safari fields. Pitch a tent in the cool-season breeze and look for wildflowers.

highlights.name: Flying morning glory (phak bung loi fa)
highlights.blurb: Stir-fried morning glory where the cook flings it from the wok across the way for a waiter to catch on a plate. The riverside show became one of the town's signature dishes.

foodScene.name: Dangling-legs noodles (kuai tiao hoi kha)
foodScene.note: Noodle shops on the Nan River where you sit on a bench with your legs hanging over the bank. You'll find this atmosphere around the front of Wat Yai.

foodScene.name: Flying morning glory (phak bung loi fa)
foodScene.note: Fire-fried morning glory tossed from the wok, eaten with hot rice. Riverside spots in town do it so often it's become a local landmark dish.

foodScene.name: Sun-dried bananas (kluai tak)
foodScene.note: A well-known souvenir from Bang Krathum district, sun-dried until sweet and chewy. Grab some to take home at souvenir shops and roadside stalls.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, sai ua, and crispy pork (khaep mu) are easy to find at shops in town — lower-northern flavors mixed with central Thai.

foodScene.name: Sukhothai noodles and street food
foodScene.note: Around the markets and town streets you'll find Sukhothai noodles, rice-and-curry shops, and snacks to graze on at local prices.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: The town center and the area near the university have plenty of small cafes — a good place to sip a coffee and rest after walking around.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot)
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for Phitsanulok locals, with several places to choose from at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Evening market by the Nan River
foodScene.note: The riverside market and walking street have snacks, sweets, and local dishes to graze on while you catch the cool breeze.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat Woramahawihan (Wat Yai)
attractions.blurb: The city temple that houses the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat, a beautiful and revered Buddha image, and the province's most important place to pay respects.

attractions.name: Nan riverfront and walking street
attractions.blurb: A riverside walk through the center of town with an evening market — stroll in the breeze and eat dangling-legs noodles and snacks on the bank.

attractions.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla National Park
attractions.blurb: The mountains around Nakhon Thai with the cracked-rock field, Pha Chu Thong cliff, waterfalls, and wild cherry blossoms in the cold season. There's camping.

attractions.name: Thung Salaeng Luang National Park
attractions.blurb: A wide savanna grassland with pine forest, where people camp in the cool-season breeze and look for seasonal wildflowers.

attractions.name: Kaeng Sopha Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A big multi-tiered waterfall in Wang Thong district, strong and pretty in the rainy season. A good stop to break the drive up the mountains.

attractions.name: Chan Palace (Phra Racha Wang Chan)
attractions.blurb: A historical site that was once a palace and the birthplace of King Naresuan, sitting along the Nan River in town.

attractions.name: Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum
attractions.blurb: A museum holding a huge collection of folk tools and everyday objects, showing lower-northern life in the past in fine detail.

attractions.name: Khao Samo Khlaeng
attractions.blurb: A low hill near town with temples and a viewpoint over Phitsanulok — a good stop to head up, pay respects, and take photos.
